question: ACS580 is showing fault 2330. What is it and what should I check first?
answer_gist: Earth leakage: load unbalance typically caused by an earth fault in the motor or motor cable. Check for power factor correction capacitors or surge absorbers in the motor cable, then measure insulation resistance of motor and motor cable.

question: What causes fault 2381 IGBT overload on an ACS580 and how do I clear it?
answer_gist: Excessive IGBT junction-to-case temperature, which can be triggered by a short circuit in the motor cable. Check the motor cable, ambient conditions, air flow and fan operation, heatsink fins for dust, and motor power against drive power.

question: Drive trips on 3220. What does DC link undervoltage mean?
answer_gist: Intermediate circuit DC voltage is not sufficient because of a missing supply phase, a blown fuse, or a fault in the rectifier bridge. Check supply cabling, fuses and switchgear.

question: Fault 3385 autophasing failed on a permanent magnet motor. What now?
answer_gist: The autophasing routine failed. Try other autophasing modes via parameter 21.13, confirm the motor ID run completed successfully, confirm the motor is not already turning when autophasing starts, and check that parameter 99.03 Motor type is set to Permanent magnet motor.

question: What is fault 7122 and which parameters tune it?
answer_gist: Motor overload: continuous average motor current is above the defined motor nominal current. Check that motor rotation is not obstructed, consider whether motor nominal torque is adequate, and adjust the motor overload parameters 35.51...35.53 and 35.55...35.56.

question: Getting fault 7181 brake resistor on an ACS580.
answer_gist: Brake resistor broken or not connected. Check that a brake resistor has been connected, check its condition, and check its dimensioning.

question: What is the tightening torque for the PE ground lug on an ACS580-01 frame R1?
answer_gist: 4.0 N*m (2.9 lbf*ft) for the PE ground lug, which is the same lug across frames R1, R2 and R3. Maximum PE wire size 2.5/2.5 mm2 (14 AWG).

question: How much do I derate an ACS580 installed at 2500 m altitude?
answer_gist: Above 1000 m the derating is 1% for every 100 m, up to 4000 m. At 2500 m that is 15 percentage points, so the derating factor k is 0.85 applied to the rating-table current.

question: Can I recover some altitude derating if my cabinet runs cooler than 40 C?
answer_gist: Yes. Below +40 C the derating can be reduced by 1.5 percentage points for every 1 C of reduction. The worked example in the manual: at 30 C the derating factor is 1 - 1.5% x 10 = 0.85.

question: I am swapping an ACS550 frame R6 for an ACS580. Does my existing cable still fit?
answer_gist: No, not at the top end. ACS550 R6 accepts up to 350 MCM stranded; ACS580 R6 accepts only up to 300 MCM. Cable at the ACS550 maximum will not land in the ACS580 terminal.
section: Cable sizes and power loss data

question: On a frame R1 replacement, how does the maximum cable size compare between ACS550 and ACS580?
answer_gist: It goes the other way on R1: ACS550 R1 takes up to 8 AWG stranded, ACS580 R1 takes up to 10 AWG. The ACS580 accepts a smaller maximum conductor on this frame.
section: Cable sizes and power loss data

question: What is the contact rating of the relay outputs on an ACS880-01 control unit?
answer_gist: 250 V AC / 30 V DC, 2 A, on each of the three relay outputs XRO1, XRO2 and XRO3.

question: Which warning code corresponds to fault 2310 overcurrent on an ACS580?
answer_gist: Warning A2B1 maps to fault 2310 Overcurrent. The output current is above the internal limit, which can also be caused by an earth fault or phase loss.

question: Which terminal on the ACS580-01 supplies the 10 V reference for a speed potentiometer?
answer_gist: Terminal 4 on connector X1, labelled +10V, is the 10 V DC reference voltage. The wiper returns to terminal 2 (AI1) and the low side of the potentiometer to terminal 3 (AGND).

question: What is terminal 1 on the ACS580 X1 connector used for?
answer_gist: Terminal SCR, position 1 on X1, is the signal cable shield (screen) termination.

question: What are the default functions of the three relay outputs on an ACS880-01?
answer_gist: XRO1 is Ready run, XRO2 is Running, and XRO3 is Fault (-1). Each is wired NC / COM / NO on terminals 11-13, 21-23 and 31-33 respectively.

question: Where do I land the Modbus RTU pair on an ACS580-01 Type 4X?
answer_gist: On the EIA-485 embedded fieldbus connection shown in step 12 of the quick guide, on the control cable connection page.

question: Show me the UL/NEC power connection diagram for shielded cable or conduit on an ACS580-01 Type 4X.
answer_gist: The UL (NEC) connection diagram with symmetrically shielded cable or conduit is given under step 11, Connect the power cables.

question: What are the default I/O connections for the ABB standard macro on an ACS580-01 Type 4X?
answer_gist: Given as the Default I/O connections (ABB standard macro) diagram under step 12, Connect the control cables.

question: The drive has been sitting in storage for two years. Anything to do before powering it up?
answer_gist: Yes. If the drive has not been powered up for a year or more you must reform the DC link capacitors before energizing it. See Related documents or contact ABB technical support.

question: How long do I wait after switching off input power before touching the drive?
answer_gist: Always wait 5 minutes after disconnecting input power to let the intermediate circuit capacitors discharge, after isolating the drive from all dangerous voltage sources.

question: Can I run the motor cable in plastic conduit?
answer_gist: It is allowed in NEC installations, including underground and in wet locations, but non-metallic conduit (Type LFNC) will not suppress EMC noise. Continuously conductive metallic conduit (EMT, RMC or LFMC) grounded at both ends is preferred, and each motor needs its own conduit run.

question: Is it safe to work on the drive if the motor is still spinning?
answer_gist: No, not with a permanent magnet motor. A rotating permanent magnet motor energizes the drive, including its input and output terminals, even with input power removed.

question: How much clearance do I need under an ACS580 frame R6 when replacing an ACS550?
answer_gist: Frames R6 and larger need 11.8 inches of free space below the drive, measured from the fan, which is more than the ACS550 required. This can force longer cables or a lower mounting point.
section: Low installation sites and box installations

question: On the ACS580 the safety input is called STO. What is the equivalent connector called on the ACS880, and does it behave the same?
answer_gist: On the ACS880-01 it is the XSTO connector on the drive module control unit. It only acts as a true Safe torque off input on an inverter control unit. Both families warn that a short circuit in the wiring between the switch and an STO terminal is a hazard.
